Haval H7 Goes on Sale in the Land Down Under With Two Electrified Powertrains From Less Than AU$50k
8 photos
Photo: Haval
GWM - aka Great Wall Motors - is one of the older Chinese automakers present in Australia , and the company celebrated 18 years of presence in the Land Down Under earlier this month.
The Chinese brand has decided to celebrate the milestone alongside its customers by introducing a new offer: 0.88% p.a. annual percentage rate (2.71% p.a. comparison rate) over a 36-month loan term, with no upfront deposit required and no balloon payment, for eligible models.
The latter include the Haval Jolion Hybrid, H6 gasoline, Hybrid & Hi4 PHEV, the H6GT Hybrid & Hi4 PHEV, the Tank 300 Hi4-T PHEV and 500 Hybrid and Hi4-T PHEV, plus the Cannon Alpha Hi4-T PHEV. Alternatively, customers can get limited-time driveaway savings of up to AU$4,000 ($2,800) on selected SUVs and Utes throughout October.
GWM also has a new model launch this month to complete the celebration – back in September at Australia's Everything Electric , Great Wall Motors joined other Chinese brands and introduced the Haval H7 model, promising a mid-October sales release. Well, now they intend to keep that promise and have revealed that the first batches of the all-new Haval H7 have arrived in the Land Down Under.
The company says interest is tremendous for the new H7, rising faster than for any previous GWM model, and the model has also taken center stage at GWM’s pop-up at Chadstone Shopping Center, the Southern Hemisphere’s largest shopping center. “We have high expectations for the all-new HAVAL H7, and the level of early interest shown from prospective buyers across Australia demonstrates that GWM looks to have the formula just right with this new model,” explains Steve Maciver, GWM Australia Head of Marketing & Communications.
First deliveries will start before the end of the month for the all-new Haval H7, which “offers a bolder, more confident design language, and will sit alongside the award-winning Haval H6 to further bolster GWM’s medium SUV lineup as it prepares for further growth in the country’s largest new vehicle segment.” The new SUV originally debuted in Baveno, Italy, and brings its “distinctive boxy silhouette” to Australia with four trim levels and two electrified powertrain options.
More precisely, the Lux and Vanta models are offered with both the Hybrid and Plug-in Hybrid (PHEV) configurations and GWM’s proprietary Hi4 all-wheel drive technology, which is standard throughout. The hybrid model has 182 kW or 244 hp, while the PHEV setup rocks 320 kW or 429 hp and sprints to 62 mph or 100 kph in 4.9 seconds. The plug-in hybrid model also has an electric range of 137 km (85 miles) and a kW Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) function.
Additionally, all Haval H7 models will feature a rear differential lock, the 4x4 Expert Mode, a braked towing capacity of 1,500 kg or 3,307 pounds, a full-size spare wheel, a 360-degree camera with transparent view, plus a 15.6-inch touchscreen with GWM Coffee OS featuring wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Pricing starts below AU$50k ($35k)!
